name: The Story of Cinema: From a Garden in Leeds to Streaming
description: How moving pictures grew from two-second experiments into the biggest popular art of the twentieth century, with the films, genres and film makers that drove each change.

checkpoints.name: First flickers
checkpoints.note: Inventors in France, Britain and the United States film short scenes of workers, trains and trips to the Moon, and cinema becomes a show people pay to see.

checkpoints.name: The silent years
checkpoints.note: Feature films, stars and studios appear. Germany, the Soviet Union and the United States each build a style, and sound arrives in 1927 to end the era.

checkpoints.name: Studios and sound
checkpoints.note: Hollywood studios turn out films like a factory, Disney proves feature animation can pay, and war and shadowy crime stories give rise to film noir and neorealism.

checkpoints.name: New waves
checkpoints.note: Young directors in France, Japan, India and Italy show that films can be personal and cheap, and television pushes cinema to be bolder.

checkpoints.name: The blockbuster age
checkpoints.note: Directors like Coppola, Spielberg and Lucas bring big ideas and then big summer hits, and Hollywood turns toward franchises.

checkpoints.name: A global screen
checkpoints.note: Computer animation, digital effects and cheap video cameras open film to the whole world, from Lagos to Seoul, and streaming changes how films are watched.
